prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Labour Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (Britain forward, not back)

Core vision
- Apply enduring Labour values to a changing world: opportunity and security for all.
- Embed a new progressive consensus: economic dynamism with social justice; universal services, personalised to need; rights matched by responsibilities; active global engagement.

Record since 1997
- Economy: Longest period of uninterrupted growth; lowest unemployment in 30 years; inflation and interest rates low; 2 million more in work; over 1 million new homeowners; minimum wage and tax credits cut poverty (2m fewer children and nearly 2m fewer pensioners in absolute poverty).
- Public services: NHS spending more than doubled; 79k more nurses, 27k more doctors; deaths from heart disease down 27%, cancer down 12%. Education funding up £1,000 per pupil; 28k more teachers; primary results among world’s best.
- Crime: Overall down 30%; record police numbers; ASBOs and penalties tackling antisocial behaviour.
- Global: EU leadership, doubled aid, restart of trade talks, first national greenhouse gas trading.

Economy and jobs
- Maintain stability: 2% inflation target; fiscal rules; no rise in basic/top income tax rates; no VAT on essentials.
- Efficiency savings to fund services; pro-enterprise tax regime (low corporation tax, R&D credits).
- Full employment goal (80% employment rate); strengthen welfare-to-work; reform Incapacity Benefit with support and expectations.
- Skills and science: raise R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014; back manufacturing and SMEs; green technology growth.
- Competitive markets and smart regulation; energy mix including renewables, nuclear, clean coal; consumer protections (payments, unclaimed assets).
- Transport: >£180bn public investment to 2015; rail upgrades, Crossrail funding solution, high-speed feasibility; road capacity and management, explore national road pricing; free off-peak local buses for over-60s/disabled.

Opportunity and fairness
- Education: Personalised learning; every secondary an independent specialist school; at least 200 Academies by 2010; Building Schools for the Future renewal; stronger discipline; 14–19 diplomas, more apprenticeships; EMAs; higher education expansion with fees capped at £3,000 and bursaries.
- Crime and security: Neighbourhood policing teams nationwide; more CSOs; tougher action on alcohol-fuelled disorder; expand drug testing/treatment; Serious Organised Crime Agency; stronger sentences on violent/weapon offences; offender management to cut reoffending.
- Immigration/asylum: Points-based system prioritising skills; English for settlement; employer penalties; biometrics, e-borders, ID cards; faster, fairer decisions.
- NHS: Spending to triple by 2008; maximum 18 weeks referral-to-treatment by 2008; patient choice of hospital; GP-led commissioning; community hospitals; independent/voluntary providers to add capacity; MRSA action; dentistry review; public health—better school food, clear labelling, smoking restrictions, health trainers.
- Older people: Pension Credit lifts incomes; winter fuel/council tax help; free off-peak bus travel; seek cross-party pensions settlement (Pensions Commission); end age discrimination; flexible retirement; individual care budgets.
- Families and housing: Halve child poverty by 2010–11; Child Tax Credit/Child Trust Fund; universal nursery places; 3,500 Sure Start Children’s Centres; extended schools 8am–6pm; maternity leave to nine months moving toward 12; flexible working extended; boost home ownership (stamp duty threshold raised), more and better social housing.

International and environment
- EU reform and leadership; referendum on Constitutional Treaty; NATO central to defence; retain independent nuclear deterrent.
- Support democracy and security (Iraq/Afghanistan), Middle East peace.
- UN/IFIs reform; climate leadership: meet Kyoto, aim 20% CO2 cut by 2010 and 60% by 2050; renewables and efficiency.
- Development: 0.7% of GNI on aid by 2013; debt relief; International Finance Facility; fair trade agenda.

Quality of life and democracy
- Culture and sport: Free national museums; Creative Sparks in schools; community sports facilities; 2012 Olympics legacy.
- Digital: Switchover 2008–2012; BBC Trust; modernised IP; film tax relief.
- Local environment: Clean Neighbourhoods powers; recycling expansion; Marine Act; sustainable building code.
- Constitutional reform: Complete Lords reform (remove remaining hereditaries, time limits on bills, free vote on composition); devolve more to nations/regions and councils; neighbourhood powers; social enterprise support; youth volunteering; fair, controlled council tax.
- Equality/human rights: Single Equality Act; Commission on Equality and Human Rights; protect against incitement to religious hatred; balance rights with responsibilities.
